title: observability-pipeline-incident-breadcrumbs-wip
content:
Quick scratchpad / breadcrumbs for the metrics+traces/logs ingestion issue observed after 2026-02-27 deploy. Personal notes, commands I ran, snippets, hypotheses and next steps.

Summary / symptoms:
- Around 2026-02-27 18:40 UTC we saw a drop in service-level metrics for route /api/generate (prod-us-west). Dashboards showed ~0.2x of expected metrics (error and latency metrics still present but request_count dropped).
- Traces for that route were largely missing (trace sampling rate looked correct in config). Traces that did arrive had long delays before ingestion (10s+).
- Logs from the same services still present in app logs, but log ingestion to ES index observability-logs had lag and some 413/connection errors from collector.
- Correlated with a spike in collector CPU/mem and increased Kafka consumer lag on topic "observability-events-v2".

Timeline (rough):
- 2026-02-27 17:50 UTC: Canary deploy finished for svc-gateway (rollout/2026-02-27-17:30).
- 2026-02-27 18:35 UTC: Alerts triggered for metrics drop (pager).
- 2026-02-27 18:40 UTC: Confirmed missing traces in tracing UI for requests after 18:35.
- 2026-02-27 18:50 UTC: Restarted collector pod (collector-az1-2) as a quick mitigation -> short improvement but lag returned.

Commands I ran / useful snippets:
- kubectl logs -n observability collector-az1-2 --since=2h | tail -n 200
  -> repeated: "OTLP ingestion error: http status 413 Payload Too Large" and occasionally "TLS handshake error: EOF"

- kubectl top pod -n observability | grep collector
  -> collector pods at 95% CPU, mem 78%.

- kafka-consumer-groups.sh --bootstrap-server kafka-main:9092 --describe --group obs-collector-group
  -> consumer lag jumped to ~120k for partition 3-7 of observability-events-v2

- curl -v -X POST https://collector.internal:4318/v1/traces -H 'Content-Type: application/x-protobuf' --data-binary @sample-trace.pb
  -> HTTP/1.1 413 Payload Too Large

- grpcurl -insecure -proto otlp.proto collector.internal:4317 opentelemetry.proto.collector.trace.v1.TraceService/Export < sample-req.json
  -> connection ok but server returned RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED in some attempts

- tcpdump -i eth0 port 4318 -w /tmp/collector-4318.pcap (short capture) -> saw large bursts of batches from svc-gateway (many > 1MB)

- aws s3 ls s3://obs-archives/2026/02/27/ --human-readable --summarize
  -> a few large files created by batch-archiver at ~18:30 (not sure related)

Key log/error snippets:
- collector logs:
  2026-02-27T18:36:12Z WARN otlp http_ingest.go:63 "Payload Too Large" path=/v1/traces size_bytes=1451200 client=10.2.4.15
  2026-02-27T18:36:12Z ERROR otlp http_ingest.go:78 "failed to process batch" err="payload too large"
  2026-02-27T18:37:00Z ERROR otlp tls.go:45 "TLS handshake error" err="EOF" remote_addr=10.2.5.33:52340

- gateway app logs (svc-gateway):
  2026-02-27T18:34:59Z DEBUG exporter/otlp.go:112 "exporting trace batch" batch_size=350 total_bytes=1654325
  2026-02-27T18:34:59Z WARN exporter/otlp.go:118 "batch exceeds recommended size, splitting"

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Batching/ingestion size increase: Recent change in gateway changed batching heuristics (changed max batch bytes from 1MB -> 2MB in canary PR). Collector has an upper limit and returns 413. Large payloads cause collector to reject batches -> backpressure -> consumer lag -> metrics drops because metrics pipeline depends on same topic ingestion ordering.
2) Resource exhaustion: Collector pods maxed CPU/mem leading to TLS handshake failures and intermittent RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED responses. Autoscaler did not spin up quickly enough due to HPA config (cpu target too low).
3) Network/transient issue between AZs causing TLS flaps amplified by bigger batch sizes.
4) Upstream Kafka broker issues (but broker metrics look normal except increased lag on that topic).

Immediate mitigations tried and effect:
- Restarted collector pods -> temporary improvement (~5min) then lag returned. Suggests transient recovery but underlying load still present.
- Rolled back gateway batching change on canary -> saw decrease in large-batch traces in tcpdump, but collector still saw some 413s (maybe older queued clients or other services still sending large batches).
- Scaled collector statefulset to +2 replicas manually (kubectl scale sts collector --replicas=6) -> consumer lag decreased slowly.

Open next actions / TODOs:
- Short term (now):
  - Force immediate consumer parallelism: increase consumers for obs-collector-group (distribute partitions) and ensure collectors are online.
  - Add a temporary reverse-proxy in front of collector to drop/buffer oversized requests and return 429 instead of 413 to signal clients to backoff. (Priya volunteered to prototype).
  - Patch gateway to enforce client-side max batch bytes=1MB and add logging for batch split events.
\- Check HPA for collector and increase target CPU to 60% temporarily so HPA scales earlier.

- Medium term:
  - Add server-side config validation in collector to accept larger but chunk on ingestion, or accept but stream to Kafka in smaller chunks to avoid 413.
  - Add better alerting: detect sudden increase in average batch_size and trigger an alert before consumer lag rises.
  - Run load test that simulates batched traces from gateway to validate new heuristics.

- Long term:
  - Rework ingestion path to be more buffer-friendly (s3-chunk intermediate or redis queue) and decouple large batch acceptance from immediate Kafka writes.

Questions to verify / notes: 
- Who changed batching heuristics? Check PRs around Feb 25-27 in gateway repo -> linked PR in metadata.
- Need audit of client libraries: several services use shared exporter library, verify version changes.
- Confirm whether metrics pipeline is coupled to same Kafka topic or uses different path (I think metrics aggregator writes to observability-metrics topic, but our consumer is shared).

Links and artifacts (duplicates above):
- GH PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/collector/pull/456 (collector side mitigation WIP)
- Gateway PR candidate: https://github.com/redwood-inference/gateway/pull/212
- Jira ticket: JIRA-789
- Confluence doc: https://confluence.redwood.company/display/OBS/ingestion-pipeline

Random notes / brain dump:
- "Payload Too Large" correlates tightly with batch_size>1MB, but some 413s occurred at ~1.4MB and others at 900KB (maybe compression difference).
- Need to confirm if OTLP compression negotiation mismatch could be causing larger compressed sizes -> collector not handling content-encoding properly.
- Look at ALB timeouts and keepalive settings between svc-gateway and collector (TLS EOFs).

Immediate owner / who to ping:
- Priya (obs infra) -> collector config + HPA
- Alex (gateway) -> revert/enforce batch size client side
- Luca (platform-sre) -> check Kafka broker and networking

Notes to self: make a short playbook after triage for next time (steps to scale collectors, check kafka lag, quick revert PR).

End of scratchpad.
